title: Arrays are shared, not copied
prompt: A number handed to a function is a copy; an array is not. with_item_added hands its array to a helper, `add_item`, which puts the number `99` on the end, and the original comes back with the 99 in it. [1, 2] becomes [1, 2, 99].
hints: add_item takes the array and appends 99; with_item_added calls add_item(items) and returns items. Both names point at the same array, so changes made through one show up in the other.
`func add_item(arr):` with `arr.append(99)`; it does not need to return anything.

docs.name: list.append(value)
docs.what: Adds value to the end of the array. Returns nothing.
